info.title: contextosd
info.description: The ContextOS runtime's HTTP API. Request and record bodies reference the normative ContextOS JSON Schemas by their `$id`; the server also embeds them (`POST /v1/schemas/{doc}/validate`). Every body is parsed with strict ingress (duplicate keys are rejected) and every request is bound to the caller's tenant.

An independent evaluator's score of a decision, signed into the audit chain
post.description: Policy, utility and safety come from the evaluator; cost and latency are measured by the runtime from the signed decision. Refused (`evaluator_not_independent`) when the caller also holds `admit` or `dispatch`, or is the principal that admitted the run or recorded the decision, whatever token it presents. Only record ids the gateway issued for this run can be scored, and each evaluator scores a decision once.

get.summary: The tenant's revoked targets (kill switch)

post.summary: Revoke a tenant, pack, agent, adapter or capability
post.description: Kinds: tenant, pack, principal (the authenticated caller and the runs it admitted), agent (the agent id a run declares), adapter, capability. Effective for the next dispatch and admission: effects of runs bound to a revoked tenant, pack or agent, and calls to a revoked adapter or capability, are blocked before anything is claimed (`revoked_<kind>`); new runs of a revoked tenant, pack or agent are refused. Audited before it takes effect; idempotent.

post.summary: Restore a revoked target
Erase a finished run's personal content
post.description: Overwrites the run's replay case and compiled context with tombstones (operator, time, reason, digest of the removed content), audited before the content goes. Only completed, failed or cancelled runs (`run_active` otherwise). Idempotent: `erased` lists what this call removed. Signed DecisionRecords and audit entries are not rewritten.

post.summary: Assess a conformance report for this deployment
post.description: The caller supplies the report, its verification, the control evidence, the contract, features and the workflow scope. The deployment supplies its implementation identity, support declaration, the standard profile registry, the evaluation time and the trusted assessors and evidence observers configured for the caller's tenant (`conformance_not_configured` otherwise); the caller cannot supply any of these. Every attestation must carry an Ed25519 signature by the trusted principal it names, over a domain-separated digest; caller-asserted verification is refused (`attestation_unverified`). Every outcome is audited.

report_signature.description: Base64 Ed25519 signature by the report's evaluator over the report, contract and features (see contextosd::attest)

verification_signature.description: Base64 Ed25519 signature by the observer named in report_verification

evidence_signatures.description: One signature per evidence observation, by the observer it names

get.summary: The tenant's staged rollouts

post.summary: Route a share of a baseline pack's new runs to a candidate pack
post.description: A run asking for the baseline is admitted on the candidate when its routing bucket (hash of tenant and run id; a delegated child uses its parent's) is below `percent`; the run pins that pack and admission reports it as `pack_ref` and `rollout`. With `shadow`, runs kept on the baseline are also compiled under the candidate off the request path and the governance difference is audited as `shadow_diff`. Audited before it takes effect. Before `percent > 0`, the release gate runs on the named runs' replay cases plus every open feedback record's, baseline against candidate; a failing, missing or erased case refuses the change (409 `release_gate_failed` with the gate report, or `gate_cases_unavailable`), and the passing gate is recorded with the rollout.

gate_runs.description: Runs whose replay cases gate the candidate before percent > 0; every open feedback record's case is added.

acknowledge.description: Widenings the operator accepts, by the release gate's rules (per case or capability).

post.summary: Return all of a baseline's new runs to it
Reserve budget for a model call or a replan
post.description: Reserves from the run's budget ledger (the same pool as tool calls) under the run's deadline, fencing and kill switch; refused (`budget_exhausted`) when it does not fit. A replan reserves one of the run's replan allowance.

post.summary: Settle a usage reservation
post.description: Reported by a metering principal (`meter` scope, without admit or dispatch), the measured usage is charged and the rest released. Reported by the run's executor (`dispatch`, current generation), the whole reservation is charged: self-reported usage is not evidence. Measured usage above the reservation is charged as audited overage up to the run's remaining capacity; the principal that admitted the run cannot meter it.

post.summary: Save the orchestrator's checkpoint
post.description: Only the run's current executor may write. Optimistic: `expected_revision` must equal the stored revision (0 for the first), otherwise `checkpoint_conflict` reports the current one. Content-addressed and audited by digest; erased with the run.

get.summary: The run's latest checkpoint (the current executor only, e.g. after taking the run over)
The audit chain's public signing keys
get.description: Ed25519 public keys (base64url) by key id, so anyone can verify exported entries offline with `ctx audit-verify` without trusting this server. Public, like a JWKS endpoint.

get.summary: The caller's identity and scopes, and what this deployment enforces
get.description: For operator consoles: mode, support declaration, store, which fact services and adapters are wired (names only: no endpoint, credential or environment variable), resolved guards, audit signing and retention, plus the caller's tenant, principal and scopes and the tenant's loaded packs. Any authenticated caller.

get.summary: The caller tenant's loaded Context Packs
get.description: Every Context Pack this deployment pinned for the caller's tenant, in full, by pack reference.

get.summary: The configuration this replica runs
get.description: Its TOML text, the digest of that text, the effective configuration with defaults and mode-dependent values resolved, and posture findings. The file holds no secrets by design; `config` is a deployment-administration scope.

post.summary: Dry-run a proposed configuration
post.description: Parsed and checked exactly as at startup (files and environment variables it names are checked only when a server starts with it), then diffed against the running configuration with each change classified as `tightens`, `loosens` or `changes`. Nothing is stored or audited: run it in CI against a pull request and require approval of any loosening.

200.description: The analysis (`valid` false with `errors` when it does not validate)

post.summary: File an operator correction or override against a run
post.description: From an independent reviewer (`evaluate`, neither `admit` nor `dispatch`, not the run's admitter). Bound to the run, its trace and optionally a decision of it; the run's replay case becomes the replay obligation. Audited (summary by digest).

get.description: Read-only. Resource digest is SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON resource string. Capacity covers only mediated calls sharing the tenant and store. Unknown exposure never expires.

put.summary: Correct what the run's principal authorized (narrow, or widen with confirmation)
put.description: Replaces the run's own task authorization; inherited ones never change. Narrowing (every scope narrows a current one, reads no less scoped, `ask` not replacing `deny`) needs `dispatch` or `authorize`. Widening needs `authorize` held without `admit`/`dispatch`, a `confirmation_ref` and the same `issued_by`. The task reference is part of every action digest, so approvals and operation claims made under the previous authorization no longer match. Audited as `task_authorization_amended`.

expected_revision.description: The run's current task authorization revision (0 as admitted).

get.summary: Discover peer tasks in a live lexicographic page
get.description: Alpha advisory coordination. The authenticated caller must match the stored admission admitted_by. Root and members come from protected delegation lineage. All descendants can read explicitly published metadata. Claims and worker-reported evidence grant no tool authority, evidence admission or child-output acceptance. Board CAS fences revisions/epochs; separate lifecycle checks cannot eliminate concurrent stop/takeover races. Board content is erased with the root. At most 100 tasks per page. Restart from the beginning to see ids published before the cursor; reading does not acknowledge tasks.

post.summary: Publish immutable peer task metadata
post.description: Alpha advisory coordination. The authenticated caller must match the stored admission admitted_by. Root and members come from protected delegation lineage. All descendants can read explicitly published metadata. Claims and worker-reported evidence grant no tool authority, evidence admission or child-output acceptance. Board CAS fences revisions/epochs; separate lifecycle checks cannot eliminate concurrent stop/takeover races. Board content is erased with the root. Same creator/id/definition returns the current task; incompatible reuse conflicts. Limits: 256 tasks, 16 dependencies and 1 MiB canonical board, whichever is reached first.

get.summary: Inspect task ownership and conditional revision
get.description: Alpha advisory coordination. The authenticated caller must match the stored admission admitted_by. Root and members come from protected delegation lineage. All descendants can read explicitly published metadata. Claims and worker-reported evidence grant no tool authority, evidence admission or child-output acceptance. Board CAS fences revisions/epochs; separate lifecycle checks cannot eliminate concurrent stop/takeover races. Board content is erased with the root.

post.summary: Conditionally claim, renew, release or report task completion
post.description: Alpha advisory coordination. The authenticated caller must match the stored admission admitted_by. Root and members come from protected delegation lineage. All descendants can read explicitly published metadata. Claims and worker-reported evidence grant no tool authority, evidence admission or child-output acceptance. Board CAS fences revisions/epochs; separate lifecycle checks cannot eliminate concurrent stop/takeover races. Board content is erased with the root. Read the task after a lost response or conflict. Lease expiry does not establish that prior effects are safe to repeat: inspect/reconcile the prior worker operations first. Evidence refs are not independently verified.

bearer.description: An API key (configured as its SHA-256 hash) or an OIDC JWT. Scopes: compile, admit, dispatch, reconcile, audit:read, evaluate (independent evaluators only), control (operators: kill switch, rollouts, erasure), meter (usage metering, e.g. an LLM gateway), config (deployment administrators: review and propose configuration; never with admit or dispatch).

ExecutorGeneration.name: ContextOS-Executor-Generation
ExecutorGeneration.description: The generation returned by admission or takeover. A stale generation is refused with 409.

ParentExecutorGeneration.name: ContextOS-Executor-Generation
ParentExecutorGeneration.description: Required when the request acts on a parent run (delegation, closing a child): the parent's current generation.

Error.description: Refused. `code` is stable; `message` never carries backend detail. 429 and 503 were not processed and carry Retry-After.

pack_ref.description: A pinned pack reference from the server configuration

features.description: Workflow features to declare; the server derives the rest from the compiled context and refuses inconsistent declarations (`features_invalid`).

pack_ref.description: The pack the run was admitted on (a rollout may choose the candidate)

routing_decision_id.description: The model router's decision that chose the model (recorded in lineage).

model_profile.description: Which pinned model_profile release ref (id@version) produced this decision, e.g. a pinned fallback; defaults to the first pinned.

head.description: The chain's current head sequence (0 when empty), so a reader can start from the tail

admission.description: The run's pinned admission (contract, policy outcomes, controls, limits)

evaluator_ref.description: The pinned evaluator (suite, rubric or judge) and version

state.description: The orchestrator's own state (plan, step pointer, last verdict), at most 256 KiB canonical

anyOf.description: tools/call: a governed outcome; refusals are isError with reason codes in structuredContent
Passed through from the tool: input_required (with requestState = the operation id) or a long-running task

summary.description: Null once the run's content was erased

packs.description: Pack references loaded for the caller's tenant

dispatch.description: Whether governed dispatch is enabled (fact providers configured)

TaskAuthorization.description: What the run's principal authorized for this task, fixed at admission. Every effect must fall inside one of the scopes (checked on the actual action binding with the AuthorityGrant scope rules); it only narrows broker grants. A delegated run keeps its parent's.

scopes.description: AuthorityGrant scopes; root_run_id must be the run's root run.

out_of_scope.description: `deny` refuses an action outside the scopes (`outside_task_authorization`); `ask` requires an exact approval of that action first (obligation `confirm_with_principal`).

read_only.description: Whether read-only capabilities must fall inside a scope too.

limits.description: Bounds on the task as a whole, counted across the run that issued the authorization and the runs delegated from it, on effects only. An effect that would exceed them is outside the task (`task_scope_extent`). Lowering a limit narrows the authorization; raising or dropping one widens it.

max_effects.description: Most effects the task may make.

amount_total.description: Most the task's effects may move in total. An effect in another currency exceeds it.
